title: `var` is within about 1.03 · n·u·√(Q'S) of the exact moments, by fuzz
verdict: the co-moment error stays under 1.03 · n·u·√(Q'S) over 3,000 fuzzed columns; varTol's leading constant is 160
description: Polars's `var` merges two-pass blocks of up to 128 values (ungrouped) or Welford states (grouped) by Schubert and Gertz's update (polars-var-std-streaming). Its error has the shape of the leading term of `Stat.varTol`: the computed co-moment `v · d` is within `c · n · u · √(Q' S)` of the exact `S = Σx² − (Σx)²/n`, with `Q' = Σ (|x| + 2⁻¹⁰²²)²` and `u = 2⁻⁵³`.

Fuzzed on the streaming engine, `var(ddof=0)` and `var(ddof=1)`, ungrouped and grouped by one constant key: 8 seeds of 300 columns each (6,033,974 values), sizes 2 to 20,000, shifts 0 to 1e12, spreads 1e-8 to 1e3. The largest `c` was 1.031 ungrouped (seed 2) and 0.588 grouped (seed 918, second run); every other seed stayed under 0.59. Both paths vary run to run with the streaming merge order (polars-var-std-streaming): seed 2 gave 1.031 and 0.756 ungrouped in two runs, seed 918 0.588 and 0.460 ungrouped, 0.429 and 0.588 grouped.

This is a tested bound, not a proof: no Lean theorem covers Schubert and Gertz's merge yet. Its `(mb − m)` term cancels, so a proof needs `tInv_merge` generalised over the merge's correction term (#918).
reference: D30: the reference's `VAR_*` is `S / d` rounded once (`varOf`). Polars's `stat_algo` row is `approxWithin "plan"`, tested; `StatProps`' `varTol` (leading constant 160) is what a proof would have to meet, and the fuzz stays two orders of magnitude inside it.
